title: AMB+ with a Model-A reaction: the sign of the active terms selects morphology (region B: monodisperse round arrested droplets; region C: rods coarsening into worms); no division or motility seen
summary: Active Model B+ (A=0.25, K=1) plus the Li-Cates birth/death reaction g=-u(phi-phi_a)(phi-phi_t), phi_a=-10, from a noisy uniform state (phi0=-0.4), dt 0.03, 128^2. Three arms with identical reaction and seeds: passive (zeta,lam)=(0,0), region B (-1.6,-0.8), region C (+1.6,+0.8), at two reaction settings (u=3e-4, phi_t=-0.2 and u=1e-4, phi_t=-0.4), seeds 1 and 2 (seed 0 screens agree). Region B gives the most, roundest and most uniform droplets and they never coarsen (n=39,47,33,33 at t=3000, equal or near the run maximum; CV(area) 0.37-0.44; aspect 1.03-1.05). Passive gives fewer, more polydisperse droplets with some rods (n=31,33,30,26; CV 0.46-0.56; aspect up to 1.57). Region C elongates droplets and, at the higher supersaturation, coarsens them into a worm labyrinth (n falls 33->6 and 38->7; CV 1.43-1.53; aspect 2.3-2.4). In no arm did a droplet split, and no droplet moved: region B activity suppresses the elongation that is the first step of Li-Cates splitting, and region C elongation leads to merging, not pinching. Single-droplet probes with a second fuel field also gave no motion (activity zeta proportional to fuel, or 1.5-fuel, Dc=0.3; interface chemotaxis up the fuel gradient dissolves the droplet at chi>=2 and leaves it static at chi=0.3-0.8).

finding.operator: AMB+ active currents lam |grad phi|^2 and zeta (lap phi) grad phi added to Model AB (conserved phase separation + non-conserved reaction)
finding.control: matched passive arm (zeta=lam=0) and opposite-sign arm, same reaction, seeds and dt
